chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, and Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about old wine that is turned into vinegar. He said: There is no problem.

key_terms.الْخَمْر: Wine (specifically grape wine, often considered ritually impure)
key_terms.الْعَتِيقَة: Old (referring to wine that has aged and thickened)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is old wine that turns into vinegar considered pure and permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that old wine (*khamr 'atiqah*) which has naturally transformed into vinegar is permissible for consumption and is not considered ritually impure (*najis*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the transformation of a substance (*istihlak*) alters its legal status, distinguishing it from fresh wine while affirming its purity for use.
